hook: The Kohl Building of 1901, an Article 10 landmark on the site of one of Samuel Brannan's two 1853 Montgomery Street buildings.

parcel.note: Business addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the address was named in the prompting source.

historic_status.reason: Article 10 Individual Landmark, Historic Survey Result

historic_district.note: A spatial query against the historic-district boundaries returns no district for this parcel; its protection is an individual landmark designation.

structural work for a window-washing scaffold and rails

permits_note: Four of the 157 filings on this address are shown; the rest are office tenant improvements floor by floor and the mechanical, electrical and fire-alarm permits that accompany them.

narrative.lead: Samuel Brannan put up one of a pair of Montgomery Street buildings on this site in 1853; the building standing here replaced it.

historical_record.description: The Alvinza Hayward Building, designed by the firm Percy & Hamilton.
The Kohl Building was the only high-rise in the Financial District to survive, in part, the earthquake and fire.

Samuel Brannan erected buildings at 400 and 420 Montgomery Street out of the profits of real-estate investments; they were then considered ornaments of the city and evidence of confidence in its future.

building.architect: George Washington Percy and Frederick Foss Hamilton
building.completed_conflict: The assessor's roll gives 1901; this address is recorded as built 1906.
